from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        for card in axiom_cards:

        stack = Group(*[ImageMobject(asset_path).scale(0.15) for _ in range(8)])
        stack.arrange(DOWN, buff=-0.3)
        stack_title = Text("The 8 Rules", font_size=24, color=WHITE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Geometry of Data", [
            "Data lives in feature spaces.",
            "Emojis act as coordinate vectors.",
            "Adding moods creates new feelings."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/emoji.svg]
        emoji = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/emoji.svg")
        data_points = VGroup(*[emoji.copy() for _ in range(8)])
        for p in data_points:
            # Using Row B to E, Cols 4 to 6 (B004, B008)
            grid_pos = f"{np.random.choice(['B', 'C', 'D', 'E'])}{np.random.choice(['4', '5', '6'])}"
            self.place_at_grid(p, grid_pos, scale_factor=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(data_points))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#8A2BE2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line of best fit
        line = Line(start=self.grid['B4'], end=self.grid['E6'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        projections = VGroup()
        for p in data_points:
            # Projection logic
            start_vec = line.get_start()
            line_vec = line.get_vector()
            p_vec = p.get_center()
            t = np.dot(p_vec - start_vec, line_vec) / np.dot(line_vec, line_vec)
            proj = start_vec + np.clip(t, 0, 1) * line_vec
            projections.add(Line(p_vec, proj, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2))
        
        self.play(Create(projections))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Abstract spaces unify diverse systems.",
            "Structure powers AI and physics.",
            "Logic is the universal language."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        robot = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.play(FadeIn(robot))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

outline.topic: The Logic of Abstract Vector Spaces

sections.title: From Concrete to Abstract: The Intuition
sections.content: Briefly review 2D/3D vectors as arrows. Introduce the shift: what if 'vectors' aren't just arrows, but functions or polynomials? Define a vector space as a collection of objects that satisfy specific rules (Closure, Additivity, Scaling).
sections.example: Visualize a 2D arrow turning into a musical wave function. Both are 'vectors' because they can be scaled (volume/length) and added (combining sounds/positions).

sections.title: The Rulebook: The 8 Axioms
sections.content: Present the 8 formal axioms (associativity, commutativity, zero vector, inverse, etc.) as the 'rules of the game.' Use a visual table where checks mark compliance for both traditional arrows and abstract objects.
sections.example: Use 'Space-Bot,' a robot character that can only perform operations that follow these 8 rules. If an operation breaks the rules, Space-Bot errors out.

sections.title: Example: The Polynomial Vector Space
sections.content: Demonstrate that the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 is a vector space. Show addition (p(x) + q(x)) and scalar multiplication (c * p(x)) graphically by shifting and stretching curves.
sections.example: Represent a quadratic polynomial as a set of 'DNA markers' (coefficients a, b, c). Show how adding two polynomials is just adding their DNA markers, proving they behave like standard vectors.

sections.title: Application: The Geometry of Data
sections.content: Connect abstract spaces to real-world applications. Explain that machine learning represents images or documents as vectors in high-dimensional 'feature spaces.'
sections.example: Imagine a 'Mood-Space' where different emojis are vectors. The sum of a 'Happy' vector and a 'Party' vector creates a new 'Ecstatic' vector in the same abstract space.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Abstract vector spaces are not about 'shapes,' but about 'logical structure.' Emphasize that stripping away physical form allows us to solve complex problems in physics, economics, and AI.
sections.example: Final visual: A collection of diverse items (arrows, waves, lists, polynomials) merging into a single 'Library of Vectors,' signifying the unifying power of linear algebra.
